articles.title: NASA, Partners Accelerate Lander Development for 2028 Moon Missions
articles.description: As NASA returns humans to the lunar surface and establishes a long-term presence on our closest celestial neighbor, the agency and commercial human landing system providers Blue Origin and SpaceX have streamlined the designs and changed both concepts of operations for its future crewed landers. Since NASA established initial contracts with Blue Origin and SpaceX […]
articles.summary: NASA and its partners are rapidly advancing lunar lander technology for ambitious crewed missions to the Moon in 2028. These developments mark a major milestone in humanity's return to the lunar surface.

articles.title: NASA’s Artemis III Mission to Test Future Moon Lander Operations
articles.description: Before astronauts return to the lunar surface, NASA will first conduct one of the most ambitious and complex test missions in the agency’s history.  Launching in 2027, Artemis III will send NASA astronauts Randy Bresnik, Frank Rubio, Andre Douglas, and ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano aboard the Orion spacecraft into low Earth orbit […]
articles.summary: NASA's Artemis III mission will conduct groundbreaking tests of next-generation Moon lander operations before astronauts arrive. This complex test flight represents a critical step toward sustainable lunar exploration.

articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission launches toward Phobos, marking an exciting new chapter in Mars system exploration. This groundbreaking mission will provide unprecedented data about Mars's mysterious moons.

articles.title: Lumina simulation brings the early universe to life on a record-breaking scale
articles.description: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and Nancy Roman Space Telescope are revealing the universe's earliest chapters in detail. To help astronomers understand what they are seeing, researchers at the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian have developed "Lumina," one of the largest and most detailed simulations ever created of the early universe.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The groundbreaking Lumina simulation recreates the early universe at record-breaking scales, complementing JWST and Nancy Roman observations to reveal the cosmos's earliest history.

articles.title: NASA adopting Apollo's urgency to build a moon base and land astronauts within 2 years
articles.description: NASA is moving fast on its plans to build a moon base and return astronauts to the lunar surface in as little as two years.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NASA accelerates its lunar ambitions with plans to establish a moon base and return astronauts to the lunar surface within two years, reflecting renewed commitment to exploration.

articles.title: Three giant black holes discovered in a galaxy from the dawn of time
articles.description: Astronomers have discovered three actively feeding black holes inside a single galaxy more than 12.5 billion light-years away, revealing a remarkable scene from the universe’s infancy. Two of the black holes are separated by just 620 light-years and are expected to eventually merge, while a third lurks farther away. One weighs an astonishing 80 million suns, and another is growing faster than conventional theories predict.
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered three actively feeding supermassive black holes within a single galaxy from the early universe more than 12.5 billion light-years away, challenging our understanding of black hole formation.

articles.title: Astronomers may have discovered the first moon beyond our Solar System
articles.description: Astronomers have uncovered evidence of a bizarre, potentially historic discovery: the first moon ever detected beyond our Solar System. Unlike familiar moons, this mysterious object is at least as massive as Jupiter and orbits a brown dwarf, which itself circles a star. The unusual arrangement challenges traditional definitions of planets and moons, leaving scientists unsure what to call it.
articles.summary: Astronomers have uncovered compelling evidence of what may be the first moon ever detected beyond our Solar System, representing a landmark discovery in exoplanet science.

articles.title: NASA’s asteroid Bennu samples reveal a 4.5-billion-year-old secret
articles.description: Tiny samples from asteroid Bennu are rewriting scientists' understanding of how our Solar System formed. New evidence suggests that Bennu was born where material from the inner and outer Solar System mixed, with Jupiter playing a surprising role in shaping its formation.
articles.summary: Samples collected by NASA's OSIRIS-REx mission from asteroid Bennu reveal new insights into the 4.5-billion-year-old processes that shaped our Solar System's formation.

articles.title: NASA’s Swift Mission Ends, Leaves Behind Scientific Bonanza
articles.description: NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory has ended its science mission now that the spacecraft is orbiting less than 171 miles (275 kilometers) above Earth’s surface. The greater atmospheric drag at this height prevents the satellite’s telescopes from steadily gazing at their astronomical targets. Swift conducted its final observation on Oct. 20. It is expected to […]
articles.summary: NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory concludes its remarkable science mission after years of groundbreaking observations. The spacecraft leaves behind an extraordinary legacy of discoveries about the universe's most violent events.

articles.title: RS-25 Engine Tests at NASA Stennis
articles.description: Teams at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi tested RS-25 engine No. 10001 on Oct. 21, 2026. The hot fire test lasted for almost eight-and-a-half minutes (500 seconds), the same amount of time RS-25 engines fire during launch of NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket, with a 111% power level. For each […]
articles.summary: NASA teams successfully tested the RS-25 engine at Stennis Space Center, advancing propulsion technology for future deep space missions. These tests validate critical systems for humanity's journey beyond Earth orbit.

articles.summary: A stunning nebula reveals the cosmic process of star formation in action. These stellar nurseries showcase the magnificent chemistry and physics that birth new suns.

articles.title: Celebrating BepiColombo, three words at a time
articles.description:
Video: 
			00:03:32
				
BepiColombo launched on 20 October 2018. This year, the anniversary is special. After eight years of travelling through the inner Solar System, the ESA/JAXA mission will arrive at Mercury on 9 December, 2026. To celebrate, mission team members were asked to describe BepiColombo in just three words.
Their answers capture the character of the mission and the people behind it. Complex, collaborative and transformative are among the words chosen, reflecting both the demanding journey to Mercury and the international teamwork that has made it possible. Together, their words offer a personal snapshot of BepiColombo as it approaches its long-awaited destination.
articles.summary: BepiColombo celebrates a major anniversary as it continues its remarkable journey to Mercury. This collaborative ESA-JAXA mission represents the pinnacle of international space exploration partnership.

articles.title: Euclid discovers new comet
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.
articles.summary: The Euclid space telescope discovers its first previously unknown comet, demonstrating the mission's exceptional capability to uncover hidden cosmic objects. This discovery highlights the power of modern space-based observatories.

articles.title: Where winds blow and lava flows
articles.description:

articles.summary: Witness the dynamic geological wonders of a planetary body where powerful winds interact with volcanic landscapes. This showcase of planetary processes reveals the diverse and fascinating worlds in our solar system.

articles.title: Mars moon lander set to launch on 19 October
articles.description:
The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch into space on a H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026 (20:41 BST / 21:41 CEST on 19 October 2026). MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. 
MMX is led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), in collaboration with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the French space agency (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the European Space Agency (ESA).
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration mission prepares for launch toward Mars's intriguing moon Phobos. This ambitious Japanese-led exploration will unlock new scientific understanding of the Mars system.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: The Solar Orbiter spacecraft solves the mystery of magnetic switchbacks in the solar wind, revealing fundamental physics of the Sun. This discovery advances our understanding of solar dynamics and space weather.

articles.title: Rare Lunar Meteorites Could Fill Gaps In Moon’s Evolution
articles.description: Almost all meteorites come from asteroids, not the Moon or Mars.  But after decades of analysis of the Apollo samples, researchers still rely on lunar meteorites to better understand our anomalously large Moon.
articles.summary: Rare lunar meteorites discovered on Earth could provide crucial insights into the Moon's geological evolution, complementing decades of Apollo sample analysis with new perspectives on lunar history.

articles.title: 27 Exoplanet Targets for the World's First Private Space Telescope
articles.description: Get ready for the age of private space telescopes. The Lazuli Space Telescope will launch in a few years and part of its mission is to observe exoplanets. New research presents a list of 27 exoplanet targets, some of which are very well-known and will certainly benefit from deeper observations.
articles.summary: The Lazuli Space Telescope, a private space observatory launching in the coming years, will target 27 exoplanets, ushering in an exciting new era of commercial astronomical discovery.

articles.title: JWST Reveals a Lopsided Alien World with Blistering Evening Winds
articles.description: Typically, when we think of exoplanets, we think of neat spheres floating directly in front of their star, which acts as a giant spotlight. From our vantage point, they would look more like two perfect two dimensional circles than spheres, though. But nature is almost never so clean-cut. A new paper published in Nature Astronomy from researchers at Cornell and the University of Bristol details the first-ever study of an exoplanet that is noticeably lopsided.
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope discovers an asymmetrical exoplanet with extreme evening winds, revealing unexpected atmospheric dynamics on alien worlds.

articles.title: Black holes spinning near maximum rate could split in two, calculations suggest
articles.description: Two black holes can collide and merge into one. But could the opposite happen: could a single black hole split into two smaller ones? That question is explored in a new theoretical study: "When Black Holes Admit Pair-of-pants Topologies," published in the journal Physical Review D.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Theoretical calculations suggest that rapidly spinning black holes near their maximum rotation rate could potentially split into two separate black holes, representing a fascinating reversal of the merger process.

articles.title: ALMA spots 'dragon egg' that may represent the earliest stages of massive star formation
articles.description: Astronomers identified an exceptionally tiny core that may represent an early stage in the formation of a massive star. Located in an infrared-dark area called Dragon Cloud, the core is nicknamed the "dragon egg." The paper, accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics, was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Oct. 5.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The ALMA observatory has identified an exceptionally tiny core that may represent the earliest stages of massive star formation, offering insights into how the universe's largest stars begin their lives.

articles.title: Astronomers uncover a mysterious magnetic web above the Sun
articles.description: The Sun’s seemingly peaceful regions are hiding a surprisingly complex magnetic world. Using a balloon-borne telescope high above Earth, scientists discovered delicate, thread-like magnetic structures woven through the solar atmosphere, apparently shaped by twisting motions on the Sun’s surface. They also mapped magnetic fields inside towering jets of solar material, revealing how those fields change with height.
articles.summary: Using a balloon-borne telescope, astronomers have uncovered a surprisingly complex magnetic web structure above the Sun's seemingly peaceful regions, revealing new dynamics in solar physics.

articles.title: Nearly 3,000 exploding stars challenge our understanding of the Universe
articles.description: A massive analysis of 2,884 exploding stars has uncovered new evidence that dark energy, the mysterious force accelerating the universe’s expansion, may change over time. The findings challenge a cornerstone of modern cosmology and could reshape our understanding of how the universe works.
articles.summary: Analysis of nearly 3,000 exploding stars provides new evidence supporting the existence of dark energy and advancing our understanding of the universe's expansion.

articles.title: Astronauts’ hearts just passed a surprising test for Mars
articles.description: A new study tracking 13 astronauts suggests that the human heart may be surprisingly well equipped for a journey to Mars, especially with regular exercise during spaceflight. Researchers found that astronauts' hearts adapted to months of weightlessness and handled simulated Martian gravity without major problems, offering new hope for future missions to the Red Planet.
articles.summary: A new study tracking astronauts' heart health suggests that the human heart may be remarkably well-adapted for the physiological demands of a crewed mission to Mars.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 24, 1946: V-2 rocket takes 1st photos of Earth from space
articles.description: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.summary: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photograph of Earth from space, marking a historic milestone in human spaceflight and our perspective on our planet.

articles.title: NASA lays out plan for Artemis 3 moon-lander test flight —but when will it launch?
articles.description: NASA just gave us our best look yet at its Artemis III moon-lander test flight, which is scheduled to launch to Earth orbit next year. But a firm liftoff date has not yet been announced.
articles.summary: NASA reveals detailed plans for the Artemis III moon-lander test flight, marking a major milestone in humanity's return to the lunar surface.

articles.title: Space Mysteries: Did a planet-sized object collide with Earth to form the moon? [8:42]
articles.description: A leading theory proposes that ancient Earth collided with a planet-sized object, creating the moon within a period that may have been as short as just a few hours. Space Mysteries: Did a planet-sized object collide with Earth to form the moon? | 8:42 VideoFr…
articles.summary: Scientists explore the giant-impact hypothesis, a leading theory proposing that a planet-sized object collided with ancient Earth to form our Moon.
